candidates.name: OPA/Gatekeeper admission enforcement
candidates.reason: Gatekeeper's admission context can authorize trusted Node-label mutations by authenticated caller and old/new values before those labels influence workload placement.
candidates.application_scope: Validate Node creation and updates, including adding, changing, or removing protected keys; preserve permitted self-registration metadata.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Protect policies and webhook configuration, cover cluster-scoped Nodes, and prevent fail-open bypass; failing closed also needs a registration-recovery plan. Caller-dependent checks cannot be reconstructed by ordinary audit.
candidates.date_evidence: Current v3.23.x documentation is undated; the separately opened Radar overview is dated 2021-10-27 and is post-cutoff. No pre-cutoff version was established.
candidates.translation_note: Applying these admission facilities specifically to protected Node labels is an internal-model design translation, not a claim of an existing deployed policy.

candidates.name: XACML 3.0: authenticated namespace ownership and deny-biased enforcement
candidates.reason: XACML's issuer-specific namespaces and authenticated-source checks can inform reserving placement-label prefixes to trusted writers while retaining ordinary self-reported labels.
candidates.application_scope: Authorize protected label-key writes at the API boundary, with explicit denial for untrusted writers or unresolved decisions.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: The standard's namespace example concerns policy identifiers; adapting it to Node labels requires implementation and does not require adopting XML.
candidates.date_evidence: Opened OASIS Standard dated 2013-01-22, especially sections 7.2.2 and 9.2.5.

candidates.name: NIST SP 800-162 (2014): authoritative attribute management
candidates.reason: NIST's attribute-authority, validation, and provenance requirements can separate trusted placement metadata from inventory asserted by a node.
candidates.application_scope: Define permitted label issuers and values, and preserve accountable changes to trusted scheduling attributes.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: This is design guidance requiring an enforcement mechanism; trusted attribute administration must remain outside a compromised node's control.
candidates.date_evidence: Original January 2014 PDF body and 2014-01-16 publication record opened; later archival wrapper and 2019 revisions distinguished.

candidates.name: SPIRE: independently attested node identity and attributes
candidates.reason: SPIRE's server-verified node proofs and platform-derived selectors can inform automatic registration in which a trusted controller, rather than a node's assertion, grants placement identity.
candidates.application_scope: Supply independently verified node attributes to a separate label-authorizing controller.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Requires custom integration and protected platform metadata; attestation does not establish that an authorized machine remains uncompromised.
candidates.date_evidence: Primary concepts page is live and undated. The dated Radar entry is 2018-11-14, after cutoff; it does not establish pre-cutoff availability.

candidates.name: Azure Gatekeeper pattern: a protected registration boundary
candidates.reason: The Gatekeeper pattern can separate untrusted registration input from the privileged component that writes trusted placement labels.
candidates.application_scope: Centralize label validation while exposing a limited registration interface and protecting the trusted metadata writer.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: This general pattern supplies no label policy; direct-write bypasses must be closed, and the extra enforcement dependency affects availability.

raw_response:
# Baseline B — C04

Found five references through the permitted catalogues. The applications below are internal-model translations to Node-label authorization. Sensitive-workload selectors would need to use protected keys, and authorization must cover first registration as well as subsequent changes. No deployment or demonstrated effectiveness is claimed.

1. **OPA/Gatekeeper admission enforcement** — https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/website/docs/
   Use caller identity and old/new Node objects to reject unauthorized creation, addition, replacement, or removal of trusted labels while permitting ordinary registration metadata. The input is documented at https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/website/docs/input/. Conditions include protected policy configuration, complete write-path coverage, and fail-closed behavior with a recovery plan; https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/website/docs/failing-closed/ explains the Node-registration deadlock risk. Current v3.23.x details have unknown date status. The 2021-10-27 Radar overview is later evidence, not proof of availability by the cutoff. Discovery: https://github.com/open-policy-agent/awesome-opa.

2. **XACML 3.0: authenticated namespace ownership and deny-biased enforcement** — https://docs.oasis-open.org/xacml/3.0/xacml-3.0-core-spec-os-en.html
   Transfer its authenticated namespace-owner check to label-key prefixes so only designated trusted writers can assign sensitive placement labels. Deny unresolved authorization decisions. XACML discusses policy identifiers, so this label application is an inference requiring implementation; adopting XML is unnecessary. Date: the opened OASIS standard is 2013-01-22, before the cutoff. Discovery: https://github.com/kanywst/awesome-authorization.

3. **NIST SP 800-162 (2014): authoritative attribute management** — https://csrc.nist.gov/files/pubs/sp/800/162/final/docs/nist.sp.800-162-201401.pdf
   Use defined attribute authorities, value validation, and provenance to distinguish trusted placement attributes from node-supplied inventory. Specify who can assign each protected key and retain accountable updates; sensitive selectors should rely on that protected set. This is guidance requiring enforcement code, with attribute administration outside the compromised node's control. Date: original January 2014 body verified separately from its later archival cover. Discovery: https://github.com/kanywst/awesome-authorization.

4. **SPIRE: independently attested node identity and attributes** — https://spiffe.io/docs/latest/spire-about/spire-concepts/
   Use independently verified node proofs and platform attributes before a trusted controller grants placement labels, preserving automatic registration where external identity evidence exists. This needs a custom integration and platform metadata the node cannot alter. Attestation does not prove that an authorized machine remains uncompromised. Date: primary concepts are live/unknown; the opened Radar entry was published 2018-11-14, after the cutoff. Discovery: https://github.com/kanywst/awesome-authorization.

5. **Azure Gatekeeper pattern: a protected registration boundary** — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/gatekeeper
   Separate untrusted registration requests from the privileged trusted-label writer, centralizing validation behind a limited interface. This general pattern needs an explicit label-authorization policy, protection against direct-write bypasses, and availability planning. Date: the opened entry was updated 2026-06-03 and is later evidence. Discovery and verification: the same permitted Azure pattern-catalogue entry.

The two pre-cutoff references establish transferable authorization principles, not Kubernetes implementations. Current OPA/Gatekeeper and SPIRE details remain unknown at the cutoff; their separately dated Radar descriptions are post-cutoff. Colocated endpoint sidecars were not retained as a protection against host compromise. Kyverno was explored but not retained because only label-presence checks were verified.
